title: FCP Lab in CI
bridge: Running FCP Lab in CI is like giving every PR its own preview deployment, the way frontend-ci builds dashboard-$BRANCH. Except: the preview is the whole stack (cloud, a real Rhino client, the frontend) inside one runner pod. It is built from images made once per commit, and it is thrown away after the run.
intro: Today every cloud, client and frontend push waits 20 to 30 minutes for a shared QA lock. FCP Lab boots a private copy of the stack instead. This lesson walks through five tickets. We prove the Lab on Linux, give it its own nodes and build its images once. Then we run it on every PR and move the frontend gate onto it.

picture.caption: Images built once per commit; a private Lab per run on its own node; the gate moves from QA to the Lab.

sections.h: Gate D, part 1: measure a clean Linux host (G7-09)
p: FCP Lab has only passed on Macs. Its own docs/verification.md lists Gate D, a clean Linux host, as never run. CI runners, sandbox VMs and the nightly image are all Linux, so the rest of this lesson waits on Gate D.

First, with Nave (the Lab's owner), move the lab repo into the RhinoHealth org as a private repo. Then CI can check it out with a GitHub App token. Next, launch one throw-away m8i.2xlarge by hand in the inf account: Ubuntu 24.04, IMDSv2, encrypted gp3, an auto_stop_at tag. It gets no cloud credentials, kubeconfig or VPN; install Docker Engine and Compose v2.
The ticket's script wraps the Lab's own ci/rehearse.sh and records the numbers G7-16 needs to size the runners.
sections.because: We sample docker stats while the Lab runs, because peak memory per service decides the node size.

code.file: fcp-local-lab/ci/gate-d.sh (part 1 of 2; lab repo, final name to confirm with Nave)
code.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Gate D on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 VM, plus the numbers G7-16 needs to size lab-runner-set.
# Usage: ci/gate-d.sh /absolute/path/to/fcp   (no cloud credentials, kubeconfig or VPN on this machine)
set -euo pipefail
fcp="${1:?usage: ci/gate-d.sh /absolute/path/to/fcp}"
lab_root="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)"
out="gate-d-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
mkdir -p "$out"

{ uname -a; nproc; free -g; df -h /var/lib/docker; docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'; docker compose version; } > "$out/host.txt"

# Sample per-container CPU and memory every 10 s while the Lab runs.
( while sleep 10; do
    docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}},{{.CPUPerc}},{{.MemUsage}}' | sed "s/^/$(date +%s),/" >> "$out/stats.csv"
  done ) &
sampler=$!
trap 'kill "$sampler"' EXIT

One argument: the absolute path to an fcp checkout. The machine holds no credentials.
Stop on any error, on an unset variable, and on a failure inside a pipe.
The first argument, or exit with the usage message.
The lab repo's root: the folder above ci/, as an absolute path.
An output folder named with the UTC time, for example gate-d-20261014T091500Z.
Record the host: kernel, CPUs, memory, Docker disk, Docker and Compose versions.
In a background subshell, every 10 seconds ...
... append one CSV line per container: time, name, CPU and memory.
$! is the process id of the background job.
When the script exits, for any reason, stop the sampler.

sections.h: Gate D, part 2: cold, warm, disk
p: The cold run builds every image; the warm run reuses them. Record cold and warm boot time, peak memory per service and docker system df. Note whether Orthanc, the DICOM image server (amd64 only), and the browser proof pass. The Lab's README says one source hash builds about 11 GB of images.

Turn each failure into a lab patch or an fcp fix with Nave. Rerun on a fresh VM until two runs in a row reach state: ready. Then repeat once inside an ARC dind pod (Docker in Docker, in a sidecar container) on inf-rhinohealth. The Lab's CI template warns against using ARC and dind untested. Terminate the VM at the end.
sections.because: We run the Lab cold, then warm, because CI mostly sees warm runs and the sandbox image sees cold ones.

code.text:
for run in cold warm; do  # the warm run reuses the images the cold run built
  start=$(date +%s)
  "$lab_root/ci/rehearse.sh" "$fcp" > "$out/$run.json" || echo "$run FAILED" >> "$out/timings.txt"
  echo "$run $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s" >> "$out/timings.txt"
done

docker system df -v > "$out/disk.txt"  # the lab README expects about 11 GB of images per source hash
du -sh "${FCP_LAB_HOME:-$HOME/.fcp-lab}" >> "$out/disk.txt"
echo "Attach $out/ to the ticket. Keep the lab's reports/ on this VM; they hold the Lab's own evidence."

notes.text: Two runs; the comment says why the second one is faster.
Seconds since 1970, to time the run.
The Lab's own proof (lab ci --source <fcp> --json). Save its JSON; on failure, note it and continue.
Write the duration in seconds.
How much disk the images, containers and volumes take.
The size of the Lab's home folder (FCP_LAB_HOME, default ~/.fcp-lab).
What to do with the results: attach the folder to the ticket, keep reports/ on the VM.

sections.h: A node pool and a runner set of its own (G7-16)
p: A Lab idles at about 3 GB, grows during a job, and builds about 11 GB of images. On the shared spot nodes it would starve fcp-runner-set jobs and fill their disks. So it gets its own pool. Karpenter is the autoscaler on inf-rhinohealth: a NodePool tells it what kind of nodes to start. ARC (Actions Runner Controller) runs GitHub runners as pods; a scale set is one named group of them.

A taint on a node keeps pods away unless they carry a matching toleration. The new NodePool fcp-lab has 8 vCPU / 32 GiB nodes and the taint example.com/pool=fcp-lab:NoSchedule. It has a cpu limit of 48 (6 nodes) and a short consolidateAfter, the idle time before Karpenter removes a node. It lives in a new module modules/karpenter-node-pool and a unit multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/karpenter-fcp-lab/terragrunt.hcl. Decide spot or on-demand: spot is cheaper, but an interruption makes a smoke run look flaky.
sections.because: We request most of a node per runner pod, because the Lab runs in the pod's dind sidecar and needs the node.

sections.h: Images once per commit, part 1: the token (G7-20)
p: A cold Lab build takes 10 minutes or more. Building once per commit and pulling everywhere (PR smoke, compare, sandboxes) is what makes a 15-minute smoke run possible. Add fcp-lab-cloud, fcp-lab-client and fcp-lab-frontend to multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/artifacts/artifacts.hcl with tags_immutability_enabled = true.
The reusable workflow first needs the lab repo, which is private. It mints a short-lived token from a read-only GitHub App (lesson p2-4).
sections.because: We put a concurrency group on the commit's sha, so three CI workflows on one commit share one build.

code.text:
name: FCP Lab images (reusable)
on:
  workflow_call:
    outputs:
      tag: { value: "${{ jobs.images.outputs.tag }}" }

jobs:
  images:
    runs-on: lab-runner-set
    permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
    concurrency: lab-images-${{ github.sha }}  # cloud-ci, client-ci and frontend-ci on one commit share one build
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.build.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        id: lab-token
        with:  # decide which App; read-only, on the lab repo only
          app-id: ${{ secrets.LAB_READER_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.LAB_READER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          repositories: fcp-local-lab  # final repo name to confirm with Nave (moved into the org in G7-09)
          permission-contents: read

sections.h: Images once per commit, part 2: skip or build
p: The tag is <git sha>-lab<lab version>, because the images carry the Lab's own patches. modules/aws-ecr keeps only the last N images per repo; check that N covers a week of commits. When G3 creates the ai-agents account, add its root to allowed_principals in artifacts/aws-ecr/terragrunt.hcl, so sandboxes can pull.
sections.because: We check ECR for the tag before building, because the second and third callers on a commit must not build again.

code.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with: { repository: RhinoHealth/fcp-local-lab, path: .lab, token: "${{ steps.lab-token.outputs.token }}" }
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with: { aws-region: us-east-1, role-to-assume: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActions" }
      - uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2
      - name: Build and push once per commit
        id: build
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_SHA}-lab$(python3 .lab/lab --version)"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          aws ecr describe-images --repository-name fcp-lab-cloud --image-ids imageTag="$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
          # Placeholder CLI: the lab only builds locally today; agree the command with Nave.
          python3 .lab/lab build --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --push "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/fcp-lab-{component}:$tag"

sections.h: The smoke run, part 1: inputs and the lock (G7-26)
p: This reusable workflow boots the Lab from this commit's images and runs a smoke suite. It aims at under 15 minutes. Define the suite with the BE and FE guilds: lab test <id> --suite core, plus 4 to 6 fast specs from frontend/e2e/pr/. Pick them by last week's run times. The full allowlist stays nightly.
The Lab uses its own fake seed data. No QA fixtures and no cloud credentials go into the environment.
sections.because: We cancel an older run of the same branch, because only the newest push matters and this is not a shared lock.

code.text:
name: FCP Lab smoke (reusable)
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image_tag: { required: true, type: string }
      suite: { required: false, type: string, default: smoke }  # G7-33 passes frontend-e2e

jobs:
  smoke:
    name: FCP Lab smoke
    runs-on: lab-runner-set
    permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
    concurrency:
      group: lab-smoke-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}  # a newer push cancels the older run; not a shared lock
      cancel-in-progress: true
    env:
      LAB_ID: ci-${{ github.run_id }}
    steps:

sections.h: The smoke run, part 2: boot, test, compare
p: The steps check out fcp with full history, then the lab repo, OIDC and ECR login as in the images workflow. lab up boots from the images. The suite runs the core proof and the agreed specs. It also runs the fakes' contract suites against the real client, MinIO and Celery, inside the Lab's web-service. Check with Nave how tests_api gets into the Lab's web-service.
lab compare boots main next to this commit and says whether main fails the same way. It runs only when something failed. The job summary lists regressed, suspect, and already failing on main.
sections.because: We run lab compare only on failure, because comparing doubles the cost and a green run needs no comparison.

code.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }  # compare needs the merge base with origin/main
      # ...lab checkout, AWS OIDC and ECR login as in _lab-images-reusable.yml
      - name: Boot the Lab from this commit's images
        run: python3 .lab/lab up --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --id "$LAB_ID" --mode snapshot --images "${{ inputs.image_tag }}"  # --images: see G7-20
      - name: Smoke suite  # inputs.suite == 'frontend-e2e' runs the lab's whole allowlist instead (G7-33)
        run: |
          python3 .lab/lab test "$LAB_ID" --suite core --json > core.json
          python3 .lab/lab test "$LAB_ID" --suite frontend-e2e --spec not-found-page.spec.ts --json > e2e.json  # + the agreed specs
          python3 .lab/lab exec "$LAB_ID" web-service -- pytest tests_api -m contract --target lab  # path: check with Nave
      - name: Compare with main, only because something failed
        if: failure()
        run: python3 .lab/lab compare --source "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --id "cmp-$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --json > compare.json || true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with: { name: lab-smoke-reports, path: "*.json" }  # plus the lab's reports/ directory for traces

p: frontend-ci is the only fcp CI that runs on pull_request, and every FE PR queues for qa-front-end today, under the lock frontend_integration_tests_{aws,gcp}. G7-33 moves pull requests to the Lab and keeps QA for main, the nightly and releases. It depends on G7-31 (lesson g7-7), which does the same for cloud and client pushes.

Call the smoke workflow with suite frontend-e2e: the Lab's allowlist of 24 pr/ and nightly/ spec files. List the specs the Lab cannot run, such as GCP VMs or a real AWS bucket; the Lab's AGENTS.md names them. Keep only those on the QA nightly.
sections.because: We add a pull_request condition to the QA jobs, so QA keeps running after merge while PRs stop queuing.

code.text:
e2e-lab:
    name: E2E on FCP Lab
    needs: [check-changes, lab-images]
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_lab-smoke-reusable.yml
    with:
      image_tag: ${{ needs.lab-images.outputs.tag }}
      suite: frontend-e2e  # the lab's allowlist instead of the short smoke list
    secrets: inherit

  integration-tests-aws:
    name: "I&T - AWS"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_frontend-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml
    needs: [check-changes, build-e2e-app]
    # qa-front-end (lock frontend_integration_tests_aws) after merge, nightly and releases only
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true')
    # with: ...unchanged

sections.h: Move the frontend gate, part 2: one gate
p: The required gate e2e_tests lives inside _frontend-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml and -gcp.yml today, as a re-actors/alls-green job. It moves into frontend-ci.yaml, so one gate covers the Lab on PRs and QA on main. Check whether build-e2e-app is still needed on PRs. merge-frontend-coverage reads e2e coverage from QA runs. Point it at the Lab job's artifact, or accept no e2e coverage on PRs; decide with the FE guild.
Test this on a draft PR. Do not dispatch frontend-ci on a branch: that deploys over main's dev dashboard and Storybook. Ask G0 to make e2e_tests required in the main ruleset.
sections.because: We let alls-green allow skips, because PRs skip the QA jobs and main skips the Lab job.

code.text:
e2e_tests:  # moved here from the reusable workflows: one gate for the Lab on PRs and for QA on main
    if: always()
    needs: [e2e-lab, integration-tests-aws, integration-tests-gcp]
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: re-actors/alls-green@release/v1
        with:
          allowed-skips: e2e-lab, integration-tests-aws, integration-tests-gcp
          jobs: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}

quiz.q: Why does _lab-images-reusable.yml use a concurrency group on github.sha?

options.text: To cancel older builds of the same branch.
options.why: There is no cancel-in-progress; the group makes callers wait, not cancel.

options.text: So cloud-ci, client-ci and frontend-ci on one commit share one build.
options.why: The second caller waits, then finds the tag in ECR and skips.

options.text: Because ECR allows one push per commit.
options.why: ECR has no such rule; tag immutability only stops overwriting a tag.

quiz.q: The smoke run fails. What does the workflow do next?

options.text: It retries the smoke suite twice before failing.
options.why: Nothing retries; a retry would hide flakiness.

options.text: It cancels itself and waits for QA.
options.why: QA no longer runs on PRs once G7-33 and G7-31 land.

options.text: It runs lab compare against main and uploads the reports.
options.why: Compare runs only on failure and says whether main fails the same way.

quiz.q: Why does lab-runner-set request 6 CPU and 24Gi per pod?

options.text: So Karpenter gives each pod its own 8 vCPU / 32 GiB node from the fcp-lab pool.
options.why: The Lab runs inside the pod's dind sidecar and needs the node to itself.

options.text: Because GitHub runners need that much to start.
options.why: A runner itself is small; the Lab inside it is not.

options.text: To stop other repos from using the runners.
options.why: github_config_url does that; the requests are about node size.
